A.summary:
This change adds a database table, patchset_maintainer_sections, that
records which MAINTAINERS file sections a patchset touches. It mirrors the
existing bug_subsystems table. A bug's recorded sections decide who may read
its transcripts, but a patchset only had mailing list labels taken from
To:/Cc: headers. Anyone can put an address in Cc:, and those labels name
lists rather than people, so they cannot be used for access decisions.

Each row carries a source column, and only rows whose source is
maintainers_section confer authority. The default source is the least
privileged value, caller_supplied, so a writer that omits provenance
grants nobody anything.

The change includes these parts:

- A version 9 schema migration, run in a transaction, with two indexes.
  One of them is partial and covers only the authorizing rows.
- add_patchset_maintainer_sections, a union operation for ingestion. A
  series arrives one part at a time, and each part contributes the sections
  its own files touch.
- replace_patchset_maintainer_sections, which sets the list to exactly the
  given sections and prunes stale rows. It is meant for backfill.
- authorizing_sections_for_patchset, which returns only maintainers_section
  rows.
- patchset_maintainer_sections, which returns every row with its provenance,
  for display only.

Tests cover union across series parts, only maintainers rows conferring
authority, an empty patchset authorizing nobody, pruning and re-attribution
on replace, and no leakage between patchsets.

Nothing reads or writes these rows yet, so there is no user-visible or
agent-visible effect. The one runtime change is that existing databases are
migrated to version 9 on startup.
A.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL), the upsert does ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET
  source = excluded.source, so when two parts of a series name the same
  section with different provenance the last part to arrive decides the
  stored source. A maintainers_section row downgraded to path_prefix or
  caller_supplied stops being returned by authorizing_sections_for_patchset,
  and the real maintainers silently lose access to raw transcripts. The doc
  comment says add must not narrow the attribution, and the function returns
  Ok with no log. Replace has the same last-duplicate-wins behaviour via the
  BTreeMap collect. The failure is closed and nothing reads the rows yet, so
  it is latent. Fix: in the add path never lower provenance, and leave
  demotion to replace.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  add_patchset_maintainer_sections), the SELECT, per-row DELETEs and per-row
  UPSERTs each run as separate autocommit statements with no transaction. An
  error part way (busy database, I/O error, dropped future) persists a
  half-applied set: a wanted section can be missing, or a row meant to be
  demoted keeps maintainers_section and still confers authority. The bug-side
  equivalent, update_bug_subsystems, is wrapped in a transaction. No
  non-test caller exists yet, so this is latent. Fix: wrap both bodies in a
  transaction.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (create_patchset, merge of duplicate patchsets), the
  merge carries patchsets_subsystems to the surviving patchset but never
  copies patchset_maintainer_sections. DELETE FROM patchsets then fires ON
  DELETE CASCADE (foreign_keys is ON), silently destroying the merged-away
  patchset's sections. The surviving patchset's attribution is narrowed or
  emptied, which contradicts the documented union semantics, and
  authorizing_sections_for_patchset returns a false 'nobody responsible'
  result. It fails closed and nothing writes these rows outside tests yet,
  so it is latent, but the loss is unrecoverable without a backfill. Fix:
  before the delete, INSERT OR IGNORE the rows into the target, giving
  maintainers_section precedence when the same subsystem exists on both
  rows, and add a merge test. This issue was not introduced by edits to the
  merge code; it is an omission of this change.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts), the
  only duplicate re-added has an identical name and source, so the source
  overwrite is a no-op and the test passes whether or not the upsert
  clobbers provenance. No test adds the same name as maintainers_section and
  then as path_prefix in either order, or passes conflicting duplicates to
  replace, or fails part way through replace. The order-dependent downgrade
  in add would go undetected.

- [MEDIUM] In src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql (CREATE
  TABLE patchset_maintainer_sections), the DEFAULT 'caller_supplied' and the
  CHECK on source are the migration's central safety claim, but no test
  covers them. Every new test writes through add_ or replace_, which always
  bind source. Changing the default to maintainers_section or dropping the
  CHECK leaves all tests passing. Needed: a test that inserts without the
  column and asserts the authorizing list is empty, and that an invalid
  source errors.

- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections),
  the prune loop is the only thing that removes authority from a patchset,
  yet the sole replace test always passes a non-empty list containing a
  surviving name. Adding an early return on an empty wanted set, as add has,
  would leave every test passing while stale maintainers_section rows
  survive when nothing matches any more. Whitespace-padded names are also
  not exercised through replace.

- [LOW] In src/migrations/009_patchset_maintainer_sections.sql and
  src/db.rs (UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL), changes to the source column of
  patchset_maintainer_sections are not audited, while bug_subsystems has
  trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source in
  src/migrations/002_bugs.sql, which record additions and reattribution
  because source decides who can reach the record. A row can move between
  maintainers_section and path_prefix or caller_supplied with nothing
  recorded, so the commit message's claim of mirroring bug_subsystems omits
  the audit behaviour. The add path is also not monotonic in authority: a
  weaker source overwrites a stronger one, and a stronger one silently
  grants, both unrecorded. Nothing reads the rows yet, so this is capped at
  Low. Fix before the transcript rules consume the table, with an audit
  mechanism or an upsert that never lowers source.

findings.problem: patchset section add overwrites source, so arrival order decides authority
findings.explanation: Consequence: when two parts of a series name the same section with different provenance, the stored source is whichever part arrived last. A maintainers_section row downgraded to path_prefix or caller_supplied stops being returned by authorizing_sections_for_patchset, and the real maintainers silently lose access to the raw transcripts. add_patchset_maintainer_sections returns Ok(()) with no log, and its doc comment says a later part must not narrow the attribution. Reachability: UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL ends with ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source, and add uses that statement for every entry. Replace has the same last-duplicate-wins behaviour through the BTreeMap collect. The failure direction is closed, not an over-grant, and nothing reads the rows yet, so it is latent. It is Medium rather than Low because it is a wrong result in the table that decides who may read transcripts. Fix: in the add path never lower provenance, for example by only overwriting when excluded.source is maintainers_section, and leave demotion to replace.

findings.problem: patchset section replace/add run as autocommit statements, no transaction
findings.explanation: Consequence: replace_patchset_maintainer_sections does a SELECT, then per-row DELETEs, then per-row UPSERTs, each as its own autocommit on self.conn. An error partway (busy database, I/O error, a future dropped at an await) persists a half-applied set. If the deletes land and an upsert fails, a wanted section is missing. If a name stays in wanted with a changed source, such as maintainers_section demoted to path_prefix, the old row survives and still confers authority that the replace meant to revoke. The doc comment promises that a section which no longer matches stops conferring authority, and the code cannot guarantee that. add_patchset_maintainer_sections is likewise a loop of independent upserts, so an error leaves part of a part's sections written. The diff shows that the bug-side equivalent is wrapped in a transaction (update_bug_subsystems opens self.conn.transaction()), and the patchset functions are pub with no wrapper. Reachability: there are no non-test callers yet, so this is latent. The concurrent-ingestion case, where a backfill replace deletes a section that an add wrote after the backfill computed its union, depends on how the future callers are scheduled and cannot be confirmed from this diff. Fix: wrap the bodies in a transaction.

findings.problem: patchset merge drops merged patchset maintainer sections
findings.explanation: Consequence: when ingestion merges duplicate patchset rows, every patchset_maintainer_sections row of the merged-away patchset is silently deleted by ON DELETE CASCADE, so the surviving patchset's attribution is narrowed or emptied. The new table is documented as a union that grows as a series lands, and the merge breaks that. Reachability: the merge runs inside create_patchset (src/db.rs:5078) whenever more than one candidate matches (matches.len() > 1, line ~5488), which is the normal path for series parts that arrive out of order or as resends. The whole merge body (5440-5640) was read. It re-points bugs, reviews, patches and baselines, and it copies patchsets_subsystems with INSERT OR IGNORE before deleting. It never touches patchset_maintainer_sections. A grep for the table name finds only the new accessors, the migration and the new tests, and none of them is in the merge. PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON is set at line 1383, with a comment saying cascades are otherwise inert, so the cascade fires at DELETE FROM patchsets WHERE id = ? (line 5608). The existing test test_merge_patchsets_with_dependencies shows the path is exercised. Direction of failure: authorizing_sections_for_patchset returns an empty list, which the doc comment says the transcript rules treat as closed, so maintainers lose access rather than gaining it. The record is lost silently, which is a false 'nobody responsible' result. Calibration: Medium, not higher, because it fails closed and nothing reads or writes these rows outside tests yet (the commit says so), so it is latent today. It becomes live as soon as an ingestion caller starts calling add_patchset_maintainer_sections, and the loss is not recoverable except by a backfill. The analogous patchsets_subsystems handling in the same block shows the omission is an oversight. No test covers merge plus sections, so nothing would fail. Fix: add INSERT OR IGNORE INTO patchset_maintainer_sections (patchset_id, subsystem, source) SELECT target, subsystem, source FROM patchset_maintainer_sections WHERE patchset_id = merge_from, before the delete. Where both rows share a subsystem but differ in source, take the more privileged one, or the stricter one deliberately, instead of letting INSERT OR IGNORE pick by insertion order. Add a merge test.

findings.problem: patchset_maintainer_sections source changes are not audited
findings.explanation: Consequence: any change to which rows grant read authority over a patchset's raw review transcripts leaves no record, while the same change on a bug is recorded. Reachability: add_patchset_maintainer_sections and replace_patchset_maintainer_sections both go through UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL, whose ON CONFLICT clause does 'SET source = excluded.source'. A row can therefore move between 'maintainers_section' (authority) and 'path_prefix' or 'caller_supplied' (no authority) with nothing written anywhere. For example, a later part of a series contributes the same name with a different source, or a backfill re-runs the replace. The new tests even use the name 'net' with both sources. The authorizing index and authorizing_sections_for_patchset read exactly this column. Verified: src/migrations/002_bugs.sql defines trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert (line 278) and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source (line 300). The insert trigger writes an 'audit' row to bug_enrichments with action 'subsystem_added'. The source trigger fires on 'AFTER UPDATE OF source ... WHEN old.source <> new.source' and writes action 'subsystem_reattributed' with old and new values. Its own comment says reattribution 'decides whether a maintainer can reach the bug at all, so the change is audited'. That reasoning applies unchanged to patchset transcripts. Migration 009 contains no trigger, so the commit message's 'mirroring bug_subsystems down to the source column' is true for the columns but leaves out the audit behaviour. The dismissal argument that bug_enrichments has no patchset counterpart explains why a trigger can't be copied verbatim. It doesn't show an audit is unneeded, and I did not look for another patchset event store, so where an audit would live is a design decision for the author. Related defect on the same path: the union in add_patchset_maintainer_sections is not monotonic in authority. Its comment says it adds without removing, but a later part supplying an existing name with a weaker source overwrites 'maintainers_section' and silently revokes authority. A stronger source silently grants it, and both are unrecorded. Severity is capped at Low because nothing reads these rows yet ('Nothing reads these rows yet'). It should be fixed, with an audit trigger or an upsert that never lowers source, before the transcript rules start consuming the table.

B.summary:
This change adds a new table, patchset_maintainer_sections, that records
which MAINTAINERS file sections a patchset touches. It mirrors the existing
bug_subsystems table, including the source column. Only rows whose source
is maintainers_section are meant to confer authority over who may read a
patchset's raw review transcripts. The older patchsets_subsystems table
holds mailing list labels from To:/Cc: headers and path regexes, which
anybody can influence, so it cannot be used for that decision.

The change adds migration 9, an upsert statement, and four Database
methods. One adds sections as a union, for ingestion as each part of a
series arrives. One replaces the set exactly and prunes stale rows, for
backfill. One returns only the authorizing sections. One returns every
section with its provenance, for display. Tests cover union across parts,
authority only from maintainers rows, empty attribution, pruning on
replace, and isolation between patchsets.

Before:
  Patchsets had no record of which MAINTAINERS sections they touch. The
  database schema stopped at version 8.

After:
  The database migrates to version 9 on startup and creates an empty
  patchset_maintainer_sections table with two indexes. No existing
  behaviour or output changes, because nothing reads or populates the
  table yet.
B.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/db.rs (UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL,
  Database::add_patchset_maintainer_sections and
  Database::replace_patchset_maintainer_sections), the upsert ends in
  ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source. A later write that

findings.problem: patchset section add can demote maintainers_section provenance
findings.explanation: Consequence: a section stored as maintainers_section silently loses authority if a later write names it with a weaker source. The transcript lookup then returns fewer sections, and the caller sees Ok with no error or log. The failure direction is closed, so it denies legitimate maintainers and grants nobody extra access. Reachability: nothing reads these rows yet, so the effect is latent. It becomes live once ingestion and the transcript rules are wired in, and the outcome then depends on the arrival order of series parts. Proof: UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL ends in ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source. add_patchset_maintainer_sections passes each section's own source straight through. Its doc comment says it adds without removing and that narrowing is what the add/replace split prevents. The primary key allows one row per name, so the last writer wins. The commit's own replace test uses the bare name 'net' under two provenances, so the collision is plausible. replace_patchset_maintainer_sections collects into a BTreeMap, so a duplicate name within one slice also resolves by slice order. Tests: test_patchset_sections_union_across_parts repeats a name only with identical provenance, and no test writes a stronger source and then a weaker one for the same name. Reverting to a precedence-aware upsert would leave every new test green. Fix: keep maintainers_section once present, for example with a CASE in DO UPDATE, merge duplicates by precedence in replace, and add a test for a stronger source followed by a weaker one. Severity is capped at Medium because the failure is closed and no reader exists yet.

findings.problem: patchset section provenance changes leave no audit trail
findings.explanation:
Consequence and reachability: a row in patchset_maintainer_sections can change from path_prefix or caller_supplied to maintainers_section (or the reverse) with no record of the change. Two paths do this. UPSERT_PATCHSET_SECTION_SQL ends with ON CONFLICT(patchset_id, subsystem) DO UPDATE SET source = excluded.source, and it is used by add_patchset_maintainer_sections and replace_patchset_maintainer_sections. Because authorizing_sections_for_patchset filters on source = 'maintainers_section', that change decides who may read a patchset's raw review transcripts. Nothing reads these rows yet, as the commit message says, so no wrong access can occur today. That is why this is Low and not Medium. The impact grows once a consumer lands.

Verification: 002_bugs.sql holds all 11 CREATE TRIGGER statements in src/migrations. They include trg_bug_subsystems_audit_insert and trg_bug_subsystems_audit_source, which write to bug_enrichments. The comment on the source trigger says reattributing a subsystem 'decides whether a maintainer can reach the bug at all, so the change is audited'. Migration 009 creates only the table and two indexes, with no triggers. Reachability is real, because the upsert path rewrites source whenever the value differs.

The verification question has two parts. (1) Is there an audit table a trigger could write to? No. The only patchset tables are patchsets and patchsets_subsystems (001_initial.sql), and bug_enrichments is keyed by a foreign key to bugs(id). A trigger would need a new patchset audit table, or a different sink, so this is a missing design element and not a one-line omission. (2) Does the commit or a later patch say the omission is intentional? No. git_log from the target to HEAD returns no later commits, and the commit message says only that the table mirrors bug_subsystems 'down to the source column'. It reads as a schema mirror, and the 009 header comment repeats the claim 'The schema mirrors bug_subsystems deliberately'. Neither mentions auditing, so the omission is unacknowledged. The mirror claim covers columns and the CHECK constraint, and it is accurate for those. What is missing is the history guarantee the bug side keeps for the same column. A silent demotion or promotion by the backfill's replace_patchset_maintainer_sections cannot be reconstructed later. Confirmation that would close this: either a patchset audit sink with an AFTER UPDATE OF source trigger, or a note that provenance changes are intentionally unaudited here.
